clue.text: Duo expires horribly in Greek tragedy

indicators.note: horribly suggests the words duo expires are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people die gruesomely, as befits a classical stage tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges the ten letters of DUO EXPIRES into Sophocles' play about the king of Thebes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophocles' play about the Theban king who kills his father and marries his mother is the best-known Greek tragedy.

clue.text: It is enough, thought Frank Sargeson

definitions.text: It is enough, thought Frank Sargeson

parts.words: It is enough, thought Frank Sargeson
parts.note: the New Zealand writer Frank Sargeson titled the first volume of his memoirs with a phrase saying a single time suffices; the clue completes that title

explanation.surface: A New Zealand writer declares he has had sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: Sargeson's memoir is called 'Once Is Enough', so the clue's 'It is enough' supplies the rest of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: The memoir title opens with this word for a single occasion, the thing Sargeson judged sufficient.

clue.text: Gentleman holding bet is like a vision of afterlife

indicators.note: holding means the first piece grips the second inside it

parts.note: Dan is an old honorific meaning master or sir, as in Dan Chaucer
an ante is a stake put up before a hand of poker

explanation.surface: A gentleman with a wager resembles a picture of life after death.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic honorific is the one Spenser gave Chaucer ('Dan Chaucer'); 'Gentleman' looks like the definition but the definition is the closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Italian poet whose Divine Comedy depicts Hell, Purgatory and Paradise.

clue.text: Poet gets stimulus, say, with foolin' about

indicators.note: say signals that a word spoken out loud gives a different spelling

parts.note: a fillip is a boost or stimulus
larkin', with the dropped g, means messing around

explanation.surface: A poet is spurred on while clowning around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns FILLIP into the like-sounding first name PHILIP; the apostrophe in 'foolin'' prompts the clipped LARKIN for larking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hull librarian who wrote The Whitsun Weddings is a celebrated English poet.

clue.text: Did he recommend transportation for his son? Phaetons, perhaps?

definitions.text: Did he recommend transportation for his son?
definitions.meaning: Philip ..., Earl of Chesterfield, wrote famous letters of advice to his son; the clue jokes that he might have advised a vehicle
a light open one-horse carriage of this name is a kind of phaeton, so phaetons are examples

explanation.walkthrough: Lord Chesterfield, the eighteenth-century letter writer, was Philip Stanhope; the carriage is named after a later Stanhope.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterfield's family surname doubles as the name of a light two- or four-wheeled carriage.

clue.text: Vigour attributed to slaves by Leonard Cohen

definitions.text: attributed to slaves by Leonard Cohen
definitions.meaning: Leonard Cohen's 1972 poetry collection is titled The ___ of Slaves

explanation.definitionFit: Vigour and vitality are synonyms, and Cohen's book title is The Energy of Slaves.

clue.text: Vitriol from a Corneille nobleman

parts.note: Corneille's tragedy Le Cid is about the Spanish nobleman El Cid

explanation.surface: Biting criticism is aimed at a French playwright's aristocratic hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Corneille's play Le Cid gives CID, the Spanish knight Rodrigo Díaz.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol is literally sulphuric acid, and figuratively caustic speech.

clue.text: His tailor was stitched up again

definitions.text: His tailor was stitched up again

parts.words: His tailor was stitched up again
parts.note: Thomas ... Sartor Resartus means 'the tailor re-tailored', so his tailor was sewn anew

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin title Sartor Resartus translates as 'The Tailor Retailored'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish essayist wrote Sartor Resartus, whose title describes a tailor tailored afresh.

clue.text: Douglas Reeman's exterminators from 24

parts.note: Douglas Reeman wrote naval novels including one titled for warships whose name means killers, drawn from the fleet at 24

explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is NAVY, so these are naval vessels; Reeman, a British writer of sea stories, wrote The Destroyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast naval warships share their name with anything that wipes things out, and gave Reeman's novel its title.

clue.text: Charles Churchill and George Crabbe each provided one of these aspirants

definitions.text: Charles Churchill and George Crabbe each provided one of these aspirants

parts.words: Charles Churchill and George Crabbe each provided one of these aspirants
parts.note: both eighteenth-century poets wrote a poem named for a person standing for election, so each supplied one hopeful

explanation.walkthrough: Churchill's 1764 satire and Crabbe's 1780 poem share a title naming an office-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirants for office or a post are nominees, and each poet wrote a poem named for one.

clue.text: She died of her mistress's kiss

definitions.text: She died of her mistress's kiss

parts.words: She died of her mistress's kiss
parts.note: in Antony and Cleopatra a waiting-woman falls dead after Cleopatra kisses her farewell

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Cleopatra's attendant dies after the queen's farewell kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra's handmaid in Shakespeare's tragedy dies on receiving her queen's goodbye kiss.

clue.text: A best laid scheme of Steinbeck

definitions.text: A best laid scheme of Steinbeck

parts.words: A best laid scheme of Steinbeck
parts.note: Steinbeck took a novella title from Burns's line 'The best laid schemes o' mice an' men'

explanation.walkthrough: Burns's poem To a Mouse says the best-laid schemes of mice and men often go astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinbeck's novella about George and Lennie takes its title from Burns's lines on best-laid schemes.

clue.text: Italian novelist is something of a volatile visionary

indicators.note: something of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Italian writer is described as an excitable dreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Primo Levi and Carlo Levi were both Italian authors of novels and memoirs.

clue.text: Icarus-type from Susan Howatch? One of those Rich who are Different, seeking Ultimate Prizes?

definitions.text: Icarus-type from Susan Howatch? One of those Rich who are Different, seeking Ultimate Prizes?

parts.words: Icarus-type from Susan Howatch? One of those Rich who are Different, seeking Ultimate Prizes?
parts.note: Susan Howatch wrote a novel about an ambitious achiever, and also The Rich Are Different and Ultimate Prizes; Icarus soared too near the sun

explanation.walkthrough: Howatch's novels include The High Flyer, The Rich Are Different and Ultimate Prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambitious, successful person is one who soars, like Icarus, and Howatch wrote a novel of that title.

clue.text: Now it is a reworking of Conrad's Heart of Darkness

definitions.text: Now it is a reworking of Conrad's Heart of Darkness

parts.words: Now it is a reworking of Conrad's Heart of Darkness
parts.note: Coppola's Vietnam film adapting Conrad's novella has a title ending in Now

explanation.walkthrough: Coppola's 1979 film Apocalypse Now relocates Heart of Darkness to Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppola's film title pairs this word for the end of the world with Now.

clue.text: Faithful wife, vivacious too, and provider of Perfect Happiness

definitions.text: Faithful wife, vivacious too, and provider of Perfect Happiness

parts.words: Faithful wife, vivacious too, and provider of Perfect Happiness
parts.note: the novelist who wrote Perfect Happiness has a first name of Odysseus's loyal wife and a surname meaning vivacious

explanation.walkthrough: Odysseus's wife waited faithfully for twenty years; Perfect Happiness is a 1983 novel by the British writer whose surname means vivacious.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus's wife who stayed true through his long absence, and the forename of the author of Perfect Happiness.

clue.text: See 15

clue.text: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943

definitions.text: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943

parts.words: His arrival and departure were booked in 1943
parts.note: Arthur ... novel Arrival and Departure was published in 1943, so they were put in a book

explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' looks like a reservation but means written up in a book: the novel Arrival and Departure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian-born author of Darkness at Noon published Arrival and Departure in 1943.

clue.text: Nabokov's was in the dark

parts.note: Nabokov's novel ... Obscura, later Laughter in the Dark, names a darkened chamber

explanation.walkthrough: Camera obscura is Latin for 'dark chamber'; Nabokov's novel of that name became Laughter in the Dark in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's Camera Obscura names the photographic device, with obscura meaning dark.

clue.text: "… his — finesse was such, / So nice his ear, so delicate his touch" (Cowper)

definitions.text: "… his — finesse was such, / So nice his ear, so delicate his touch" (Cowper)

parts.words: "… his — finesse was such, / So nice his ear, so delicate his touch" (Cowper)
parts.note: a gap in Cowper's couplet is filled by an adjective about melody, fitting a fine ear and delicate touch

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the dash in Cowper's lines with the word that fits a refined ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine ear and delicate touch describe skill in melody, the quality Cowper praises.

clue.text: Honourable incitor of Les Six

parts.note: an egger is someone who eggs others on

explanation.surface: A distinguished man stirs up a group of French composers.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Six were six French composers of the 1920s, including Poulenc and Milhaud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss composer of Pacific 231 belonged to the Paris group of composers called Les Six.

clue.text: Contributed with over-the-top content in formal dance

indicators.note: content here means contained, so the second piece sits within the first

parts.note: contributed means gave

explanation.surface: Someone chipped in with excessive glee at a formal ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as happy but here means contained, the sense in 'contents'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately French court dance in duple time, popular in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Mother of Joe Egg gets German greeting in South Africa

indicators.note: in places the greeting within the country's letters

parts.note: Heil is a German salute or greeting

explanation.surface: A mother is welcomed in German while visiting South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Nichols's play A Day in the Death of Joe Egg has a mother named Sheila caring for her disabled daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Nichols's play the parent of the disabled girl called Joe Egg bears this name.

clue.text: Chabrol does

parts.note: Claude Chabrol's 1968 film's French title means female deer, so does are his

explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe, female deer: Chabrol's film Les Biches.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'the does', the title of Chabrol's 1968 film.

clue.text: "From the shores the winged — flies" (Pope, The Odyssey of Homer)

definitions.text: "From the shores the winged — flies" (Pope, The Odyssey of Homer)

parts.words: "From the shores the winged — flies" (Pope, The Odyssey of Homer)
parts.note: the gap in Pope's line is filled by a fleet of ships, whose sails are its wings

explanation.walkthrough: In Pope's Odyssey translation a fleet with sails flies from shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet of ships under sail, poetically winged, sails away from shore.

clue.text: John Buchan, for example, starts some Caledonian opus tentatively

indicators.note: starts tells us to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A Scottish author tentatively begins a Highland work.
explanation.walkthrough: Buchan, author of The Thirty-Nine Steps, was born in Perth.
explanation.definitionFit: Buchan was born in Scotland, so he is an example of a native Scotsman.

clue.text: Skaters' objective in A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.meaning: ice-hockey skaters chase the rubber disc
Robin Goodfellow is Oberon's mischievous sprite in the play

explanation.definitionFit: The disc hit in ice hockey shares its name with Shakespeare's mischievous fairy.

clue.text: Tactful diversions of Roger Peyrefitte

definitions.meaning: Peyrefitte's novel was translated into English as ... Diversions

explanation.definitionFit: Being tactful is being discreet like an envoy; Peyrefitte's novel is Diplomatic Diversions in English.

clue.text: Wickedness in surreal excerpt from Hamlet

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words surreal excerpt

explanation.surface: Something odd and evil is found in a passage from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's 'the dram of eale' is a famous crux, usually read as evil.
explanation.definitionFit: An obscure Shakespearean word, usually glossed as evil, from Hamlet's speech on a single defect.

clue.text: Ray Bradbury set his work very high on this scale

definitions.text: Ray Bradbury set his work very high on this scale

parts.words: Ray Bradbury set his work very high on this scale
parts.note: Bradbury's novel title is a burning temperature, 451 degrees on a temperature scale

explanation.walkthrough: Fahrenheit 451 is the temperature at which paper supposedly catches fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The temperature scale used in Bradbury's title Fahrenheit 451.
